utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The accused, same advisory as usual. Problems with interpretation, let us know. Appearances. I see no difference. Any preliminaries? All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, we are going to proceed and hopefully conclude as early as possible, and then you can go home. Madam Vidovic -- Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, yesterday we were talking about the way the column was created at Susnjari. Do you remember what you said on the 28th of August, page 873, in the French transcript, and you said, I quote: "As I said, first there were people who were in charge of de-mining the ground. Then behind them we had the army. The army was armed. They were going in front, and they were divided into brigades, so one brigade was following another." My question is the following, and it's a very simple question: I would like to know if this description corresponds to the way the description -- the column was created, is this an accurate description of the formation of the column?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be. The front of the column. It could be.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You've also stated, sir, that you were amongst the last ones in the column; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did anybody tell you where to stand or where to go or where to place yourself in that column?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were told to walk one behind the other and to follow the track of the de-miners, because it was them who put papers on the path in order for us to follow this track and we were told to walk one behind the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: But did anyone decide who was to leave before and who after. Did somebody say so many people were going to be in the front and so many people were going to be in the back?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The command went first with armed men, and then people just went randomly. There were not 100 people, but 1.500 [as interpreted], and those who were in the front were better off. So nobody paid any attention from which brigade people -- to which brigade people belonged to. The first column was able to break through, so everyone wanted to be in the front lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Madam Fauveau. I recognise Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a correction, Your Honour. On page 2, line 19, the witness said 15.000 rather than 1.500, as it has been recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. That makes sense. We take it as corrected to 15.000. Madam Fauveau, if you could kindly proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, you've stated on the 28th of August that in 1992, Naser Oric asked you to go to Tuzla. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did Naser Oric choose you to go to Tuzla because you knew the path or the route well?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it right to say that the route between Srebrenica and Tuzla was a route or a road that you had taken on many occasions during the war?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was the way from which I came to Tuzla for the first time, but I didn't know it well. There was a courier with me known as Nindza. I came with him from Srebrenica and back to Tuzla. I was accompanied by him. So he knew the way, not myself, this Nindza person from Snagovo. He knew the terrain and was leading the way.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: After this first departure from Tuzla to Srebrenica, did you go through that road again? Did you take that route again on another occasion?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we took the same road from which I came to Tuzla. So when I went back, we took the same path. Perhaps 50 metres left or -- to the left or to the right. We -- we were trying to avoid the mines.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, but my question was to know if after that first trip that you made, Srebrenica/Tuzla, Tuzla/Srebrenica, did you have the occasion to go and take that route again, once again, after [as interpreted] the month of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There might be a mistake in the transcript. The question was to know if it occurred before the month of July, 1995. Page 4, line 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Fauveau, because I was wondering how you expected the witness to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your permission, may I repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, if that makes it easier for you. I think the witness has heard what we have to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, since there was a mistake in the transcript, I'm not sure you understood correctly in B/C/S as well, so I'm going to well, ask my question again. Before the month of July 1995 and after the first trip you took Srebrenica/Tuzla Tuzla/Srebrenica, did you take that road again?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we show the witness 5D6? It's the interview that was found last Monday. Could the witness be shown that document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is the newspaper interview. Yes. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, I'm interested in the second paragraph in B/C/S. And furthermore, what I would like you to look at is the section -- the middle of the paragraph and also send paragraph in English. The journalist wrote, and I quote: "[In English] What does one ask a man who almost four years ago was one of the best fighters of the Srebrenica area who during the times of the biggest blockade came to Tuzla from Srebrenica four times as a courier?" [Interpretation] Do you recall giving this interview, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. I didn't say that I went four times.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When you left Susnjari, and I'm talking about the entire column, did someone have a map of the area?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't have one. I don't know if the command had one.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And the de-mining unit at that went ahead, did they know exactly where the mines were placed?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. I didn't walk together with them, so I wouldn't know if they had found any mines at all. I wasn't present there.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, I have finished with that section of my questions. I would like to go back in time. You said that on the 28th of August you worked in Serbia, Croatia, and Bosnia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And your last employment before the war, was it in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. My last employment was in Ruma, in a village where we went through the student house in Sarajevo. We were -- we were digging trenches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Madam Fauveau, which war? Which war? Because there was the Croatian one first.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was talking about his last employment, the last employment that the witness had before the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But which war are you referring to, the one in Bosnia or the one -- because don't forget that he was in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely. I was going to ask that the witness be shown the statement quoted 3D8. It was the statement that the witness gave to the Prosecution's office on the 24th of January, 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can someone check whether he has it in front of him? I don't see it on mine anyway. Yes. I can see the front page now, but in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]. Precisely, sir, Your Honour. I need the first page.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, do you have this statement in B/C/S in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that it states that your previous employment was as an employee in a sugar factory in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I worked in a sugar plant in Padinska Skela or Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is this your last employment as a civilian before you started work or before you became a soldier in the Croatian army [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was in Ruma as I stated right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, he never agreed with any question that suggested that he was a soldier in the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In fact, my question was the Croatian police. There must be a mistake in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Fauveau, for agreeing to that. And he has answered no, he was in Ruma. Wherever that is. Where is Ruma?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ruma is in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that when you arrived in Croatia you immediately started working for the Croatian police?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was supposed to work in construction, but since the war had broken out, there was no work so I joined the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, when did you leave for Croatia?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we spent a fair amount of time yesterday in Croatia with Mr. Oric. I am just a little concerned that we may be embarking on a similar tour, and I don't know whether the questions are going to be along the same line. If they are, we would object as that ground has been gone over pretty thoroughly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you are coming to a conclusion. We haven't come to that as yet. We're still waiting to see what the next few questions will be, and then we may as well agree with what you've said, come to the same conclusion, in which we will stop Madam Fauveau and ask her to move to another set of questions. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will ask very clear question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it right to say that your military training in the Croatian police lasted 27 days?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is exactly how long I had served there. Maybe even less than 27 days.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... correct to say that afterwards you joined a unit called Kralj Tomislav?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 4D7, please? It's the interview that he gave to a Croatian newspaper. I would like you to look at the paragraph under the heading "Dobrovoljac in the HV. So it's the second column I would like you to look at, towards the middle of the second column. Thank you very much. This is where it is. Now, as far as the English version goes, I'm interested in the paragraph right after the heading "Volunteer in the HVO." Your Honour, I would like to draw your attention to a translation error, since the original in Croatian is talking about the HV army, whereas the English translation is talking about the HVO army. And the difference is quite important. It's a big difference.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, are you able to see that in this article we can read, and those are apparently your words: "[In English] In Capljina, our 1st volunteer regiment Kralj Tomislav seized the barracks."

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not correct. That was not my regiment nor do I have any knowledge of that. I don't know what the journalist wrote, but I don't remember saying this. I'm sure I didn't say this. Maybe it was the journalist's regiment, not mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, you've testified in the Blagojevic trial before this Tribunal, and during your testimony one question was asked of you and the question was as follows: "[In English] And isn't it true that together with the volunteer's regiment called King Tomislav took part in the occupation on the JNA barracks in Capljina?" [Interpretation] And you've answered: "[In English] Yes, I did." [Interpretation] We are talking about the transcript in the Blagojevic trial of the 21st of July, 2003, page 1365. Sir, can you tell us if what you said at the time was not accurate, it did not reflect the truth?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And I will now ask another set of questions. You've stated on the 28th of August, before this Tribunal, that in 1994 and 1995 you were a member of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction: 1992 and 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And you were a commander of a unit composed of 10 men which was part of the 283rd Brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was a manoeuvre squad.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And how many people were in that unit?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if you're referring to the company or to the squad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, he has been asked and answered that question on numerous occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's correct. Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now go on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that before the war in Srebrenica or before actually the fall of Srebrenica, there were 14.000 soldiers in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Incidentally, before you proceed in line 25 of page 9 of the transcript now we have the 283rd Brigade. It keeps changing. Sometimes it's the 28th, sometimes it's the 281st, sometimes it's the 283rd. I've lost count.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I mentioned the 283rd Brigade, in fact. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown the document 3D7. It is the witness's statement given to the Prosecution between the 10th and the 12th of August, 1995. We go to page 2, please. Could we zoom in on paragraph five, the third paragraph from the bottom of the page. Excuse me, in fact it's paragraph four, but we can see it quite well. Sir, do you remember at the time you stated to the representative of the OTP that: [In English] "Before the fall of Srebrenica there were about 14.000 BiH soldiers in the Srebrenica region"? [Interpretation] Do you remember making that statement?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Does that statement reflect the truth?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were 14.000 of them, but not armed. They existed. There were 40.000 -- 14.000 of them, but they were not all involved. They were not armed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: So what you're saying is that there were 14.000 soldiers, but they were not all armed. Is that exact? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Most of them didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: At any rate, we can draw the conclusion that in July, 1995, there were soldiers in the city of Srebrenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were able-bodied men. There were around 14.000 able-bodied men.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it true that the headquarters of the 28th Division was in the city of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And the headquarters of your brigade, was it also in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992 when the brigade existed, my brigade that is, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Would you agree that the command of a division or of a brigade is a military target?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I wouldn't know. I don't understand much about brigades.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you know whether the command of the 280th Brigade was in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am afraid I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you know that in July, 1995, the command of the brigade number 280 was in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You stated that you were a member of the army of Bosnia- Herzegovina, but on the 11th of July, 1995, you were wearing civilian clothes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I wore civilian clothes from 1992 up to 1995. At the moment when I was captured I was still wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Were you wearing civilian clothes also when you were on the lines guarded by your unit with a rifle?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What's your objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this was just asked and answered. She -- the question was what he was wearing. He said, "I wore civilian clothes from 1992 up to 1995. At the moment I was captured --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop, stop, stop. Let him answer the question. The question is very specific as to whether you were wearing civilian clothes also when you were on the line guarding -- guarded by your unit with a rifle. That specific occasion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I wore civilian clothes just like my neighbours. Everybody in the villages. We did not have enough camouflage uniforms to go around. We did not have a factory, a manufacturing factory that would produce military clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Therefore, the men who were in age of combat could not be distinguished -- you could not distinguish between civilians and members of the military. Everyone wore civilian clothes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Predominantly everybody. A certain number did have camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that before the formation of the 28th Division the command of the 8th group of operations or the 8th Operational Group was in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I just told you I don't know much about the brigades, the command, the 8th Operational Group. I don't know much about that. I don't know where the main command was, where they moved. We just received orders through the courier when we were supposed to go to the line. I really don't know anything about this Operative Group or where the command moved. I'm not an expert in military matters. I didn't go to military schools.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, do you know if the men who were of combat age, if those who had been recruited in Srebrenica were prohibited from leaving the enclave?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, they could move wherever they wanted. They could go to Zepa. They could go back. The answer would be no.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I would like to show you a short video clip, a military -- showing a military gathering that took place in May, 1994, to be specific. May we see that video clip? It lasts two minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] ... assistant for affairs ... is going to now going to read the order on leaving the demilitarized zone would please come forward. The army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina command of the 8th Operations Group Srebrenica number 130-5- 5/94, Srebrenica 24 May 1994. To the commanders of all units, due to frequent cases of conscripts leaving the demilitarised zone, the degree of danger caused by such behaviour on the part of responsible conscripts in keeping with order number 02-1-784-1 dated 17 April, 1994, by the command of the 2nd Corps, I hereby order: One, a general ban on all conscripts leaving the demilitarised zone. 2, army members may leave the demilitarised zone only at the proposal of the unit commander, and if approved by the commander of the 8th Operations Group or the Chief of Staff of the 8th operations group. 3, in all other cases, conscripts leaving the demilitarised zone shall be treated as persons who have abandoned their unit, i.e., deserters. 4, sanctions as prescribed by the laws and regulations of the army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina shall apply against all conscripts who violate this order. 5, should a violator of this order be wounded or killed, his social status and other entitlements shall not be addressed by the military structures of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. 6, all unit commanders are to control all potential crossings out of the demilitarised zone within the zone of responsibility of their units and to take into custody all conscripts who disregard this order. Inform all members of the 8th operations group Srebrenica of the content of this order. Commander Naser Oric."

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, did you attend that gathering in May, 1994?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember even which unit is this.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: The order that you heard that was given on that clip prohibits all conscripts from leaving the enclave of Srebrenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Still, people did go to Zepa, and they would bring back food, salt, against the order. They would still leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you agree that in 1993, Srebrenica was supposed to be demilitarised?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And do you agree that during that whole period, from March, 1993, to July, 1995, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina still had some of its units in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they had a certain number, but that number, those people, just went to those lines where the UNPROFOR couldn't go.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it not correct to say that the units of the ABiH army were militarily active in Srebrenica in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can one say that the units of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina were active militarily in Srebrenica in 1995, before July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When Srebrenica was attacked, then people were again mobilised for defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And is it not also true that there were active -- offensive military activities taken -- carried out by the units in Srebrenica in July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The only thing that happened was people were defending their town from attacks.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could we submit to the witness the Exhibit 5D3. On page 1, paragraph 2. Sir, can you read on that paragraph 2: "[In English] In order to prevent enemy forces from sending additional forces from the Srebrenica and Zepa areas to the Sarajevo theatre, two acts of sabotage were carried out near Srebrenica on 23 June, 1995, at Osmace on 23 June, 1995, at Bijelo Stijenje near Koprivina, and the following results achieved: 7 Chetniks killed," and then it follows and follows. [Interpretation] Can you read those words?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And in paragraph 3, can you also read the following: "[In English] In order to divert enemy forces from the Sarajevo theatre and stretch them out towards Srebrenica and Zepa, a number of successful acts of sabotage were carried out on 26 June, 1995, at the following locations in the area of Han Pijesak and Vlasenica municipalities." [Interpretation] Is that what is written in the document?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And then if we can move on to page 2 of the document in Serbo-Croatian. In the English it's the very bottom of the first page. In B/C/S it's at the very top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have to articulate this properly. No. Just leave me the same page we had before. Now, your question or these last two questions, Ms. Fauveau, were consequential to a previous question or set of questions related to whether the witness would agree with your proposition that in spite of demilitarisation the Muslim -- Bosnian Muslim forces were pro-actively involved militarily in 1995. Now, my question, and forgive my ignorance, is Osmace included in the Srebrenica enclave? Is Bijelo Stijenje near Koprivina included in the Srebrenica enclave? And finally, is Han Pijesak and Vlasenica municipalities, are they included? Because to my knowledge, they are not. Osmace may be, but I'm not quite sure either.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps to clarify this issue we should come back to paragraph 1 of the document to make sure that everything is quite clear. May I first submit to the witness paragraph 1 of the document?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Witness, is it written on the document: "[In English] [Previous translation continues] ... 28th Division located in the Srebrenica and Zepa enclave although facing big problems in connection with food supplies and duties in protecting the area of responsibility in the free territories they control have decided to provide the largest possible contribution to the ARBiH in its fight against the aggressor, and with that aim have intensified their activities deep inside the territory temporarily occupied by the aggressor." [Interpretation] Is that what is written in the document?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it indeed true that Osmace, Bijelo Stijenje, Koprivina, Han Pijesak are places that are rather far away from Srebrenica itself?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Nonetheless, it would seem, according to this document, that the armed forces of Srebrenica were going to fight or be involved in offensive military activities in those places. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not familiar with this. I never heard of this. I never participated in this, nor do I know who did all this.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could we show the witness page 2 of the document. At the bottom of the page, the person -- the name of the person who drafted the document. Somewhat lower. Page 2. Sir, the name of Ramiz Becirevic is well known to you. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And Mr. Becirevic was the commander of the armed forces in Srebrenica in the absence of Naser Oric. Is that not true?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If I could see the original, the B/C/S version. I just want to make sure whether it's signed or unsigned, whether it's stamped or unstamped. And if I could -- if I could see well, while in the English version Becirevic is spelled as it should be, ending with "vic," in the B/C/S version it ends with "v-i-c-h," which is very unusual. I've never seen it like that. I need to see the original. I -- yes it is. It is now. Nacelnik staba. And Ramiz Becirevic is with "vich." Yes, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was a document that we received from the Prosecutor that was disclosed to us by the Prosecutor. I will not go into further details, but there is a document where there is no Serbo-Croatian lettering, so you don't see "ch" or "c" anywhere. In fact, there are several ways of writing the c to distinguish them from other letters, z, for example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please proceed, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just to perhaps clear this up. We do see in 1995 many Muslim documents that are spelled this way. It may be because of the typewriter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And I also notice because I have encountered this before, that this document also shows double letters like Scorpion with a double s. Staba with a double s, and I think that is something wrong. Basically it could be something wrong with -- with the type of typewriter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You'll see that more in the future with other things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. All right. It still does not explain the "h" after the "c" in Becirevic. All right. Let's continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now come to my last series of questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Yesterday, you spoke a bit about the fact that you did not have weapons in Srebrenica. Is it not, however, true that between 1993 and 1995 you were receiving ammunition and some weapons in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of any such thing. I was not present, and I didn't hear about any of that happening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The thing is that this typewriter doesn't have any -- or doesn't show any of the accents and marks that are particular to the language. That's -- and the mistakes or the double prints, et cetera, occur precisely where -- all right. Yes. Madam Fauveau, my apologies for having interrupted you again. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to show the witness a series of documents. Perhaps we could start by 5D7. First of all, I would like to apologise to the Court. I do not have a translation in English. It was one of the documents we found in the general collection these past two days, and we still have not received a translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Witness, could we perhaps see higher up on the document so we could actually see the date on the document. Sir, is it a document of the headquarters or the staff of Bosnia-Herzegovina army of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not familiar with this document. I don't know who signed it. I don't know who drafted the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why are you saying July of 1995, Madam Fauveau? Then it's February, not July. I mean, it's -- the Americans would read it that way, but we haven't got that far as yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 7th of February.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, I would like you to confirm that at the very top of the document on the left you can read, "Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, staff of the army," and then the date, 7th of February, 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And then could we see paragraph 6 of the document. Can you read there that the cargo that arrived during the night of the 6th of February was to be distributed between Zepa and Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what it stated here, but I was not present there, and I don't know if they were actually distributed. Zepa is -- was far from where I was. I was with my family at home. I was cultivating the land. I have no idea what was happening around Zepa at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, finally I would ask you to answer my questions rather rapidly. I'm not accusing you of anything. I'm just asking you to specify certain things. In this document we can read automatic rifles, landmines and ammunition. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, he's testified he's not familiar with this document, he's never seen it before and he's just testified he wasn't present in Srebrenica at the time and he doesn't know about the distribution of any of these materials. I would object to further questions based on this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Move to another question, Madam Fauveau. Objection sustained. Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the record we'd like to note our objection. This witness is in fact the cousin of Naser Oric, and by looking at this, I believe Ms. Fauveau would like to refresh perhaps the recollection of this witness to answer that simple question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: The last question, Your Honour, about the rifles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But he's answered that already. He's told the Trial Chamber that he doesn't know anything about that. So let's proceed to the next question, Madam Fauveau, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have six documents of the same type. Of course, if you believe that they should not be submitted to the witness I will not do so, however, I would like to say that on Monday, in other words, two days ago we found a large collection of about 4.000 documents in the general collection of Srebrenica that are all of this nature or type, and clearly they fall under Rule 68. In my opinion, we had never been aware of these before. We found an interview of this witness that had not been disclosed to us. We proceeded with the interrogation of that witness. Certainly our cross-examination may not be perfect, but we are trying to do the best we can with the means we have, and I would like to ask for your permission to pursue, but of course I will comply with your decision if you feel that I should not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... seen the other documents. Let's see them first, see what they are, and then if it's -- your question is along the same line as the previous one, we will stop you, because if he has already stated that he was -- he had no knowledge of such weapons at the time because he wasn't even there, what's the point of putting more questions to him? Unless you can prove that he is not telling us the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Witness, you were a cousin of Naser Oric; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had another 60 relatives by the last name of Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you have contact with your cousin during the war?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not very many, because I lived in Lehovici and not in Potocari, which is an hour and a half away if you go on foot. So I didn't have many contacts.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Nonetheless, you knew that in July, 1995, Naser Oric was not in Srebrenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And do you know where he was?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We heard that he had left for Tuzla with some other men, that they had gone to have -- to undergo some training.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it not true that he left for Tuzla by helicopter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is directly repetitive of the testimony that was received yesterday concerning Naser Oric's absence and his mode of transportation from the enclave, and this witness's knowledge or lack thereof concerning that mode of transportation. That's my recollection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Your recollection is almost correct. What was put to him yesterday was the reference from the article in this Croatian paper in which it was stated that some commanders had been airlifted to -- to Tuzla. There was an accident with one of the helicopters, and Naser stayed behind, but he was not put any questions -- was not asked any questions on those events. So you may proceed -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, would you answer my question? Is it true that ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau. Let me have a look at your question. Yes. Because between your question -- I think you should repeat your question, because we have all lost track of it basically.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell me, did you know that Naser Oric left for Tuzla by helicopter?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at first, but later on I heard that he went to Zepa and that he was transferred by helicopter. I didn't know at first. Later on, everyone spoke about it publicly, that he had left for Zepa probably by helicopter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Zepa or Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To Zepa and then on by helicopter.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I can clear it up. It will be my last question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you mean Naser Oric left from Srebrenica to Zepa by land or by foot or in a vehicle and then took a helicopter in Zepa to go from Zepa to Tuzla? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, because I can see that helicopters landed in Zepa. I'm sure they didn't land in Srebrenica, because the UNPROFOR would have seen them. So he probably left from Zepa by helicopter. It was not possible to leave by helicopter from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness. I have no other questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic for General Gvero. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Oric, I will try to formulate my questions so that you can give a yes or no answer and so that we can wrap up this questioning. Mr. Oric, in your testimony before this Court, you stated that you returned to Srebrenica in mid-1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you returned, Srebrenica was surrounded, and the population was organised into Territorial Defence units for defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: These units were organised according to a territorial principle. Each village had a unit for the purpose of defending that village, and if needed, they were assisted by others; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Since you are a native of Lehovici, I presume that you had joined a unit from Jaglici and Susnjari.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from the surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that some groups of villages were formed into one unit, and I will now list the names of the territorial units and you can say if I am -- if this is accurate: Territorial Defence Glogova?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just a moment. He hasn't answered yes to the general question first. It was put to you, Witness, that some groups of villages were formed into one unit. Do you agree to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Then proceed now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Oric, the Territorial Defence unit of Glogova, Potocari Territorial Defence unit?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Territorial Defence unit Kragljivoda?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that area. It is quite removed from where I was. I didn't go there during the war, but I presume there was a unit there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Territorial Defence Suceska?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Territorial Defence Susnjari and Jaglici?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Susnjari, Jaglici, Babuljice, Vlahovici, Brosevici, all of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Were in one unit? Were grouped under one unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And how was that unit known, as Jaglici-Susnjari, or some other name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There -- there was no name for that Territorial Defence unit, Your Honour. We just went to the lines to man them, but later on the units were formed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let me repeat. Susnjari, Jaglici. If you could repeat what you said, the following villages, since the --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Babuljice, Vlahovici, Brosevici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Babuljice?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Babuljice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And the commander of this unit was Sedik Ademovic or Sidik Ademovic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of other villages such as Biljeg, Skenderivici and Osmace, that they all were formed into units?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. They probably did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let's me repeat. The transcript does not -- it is not in the transcript Skenderivici, Biljeg. Mr. Oric, the commander of the Suceska Territorial Defence was Zulfo --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact name. I didn't go there from my own village and from Potocari. I went only once.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But you know that Zulfo Tursunovic was the head of some of these units?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And Ejub Golic was the head of the unit from Glogova; right?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What about Cerska? Was it Semso Salihovic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, these men that I have just mentioned, they were in Srebrenica in 1992 and 1993 when fighting was going on in the outskirts?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And these men stayed on in Srebrenica up to 1995 together with yourself?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And also the units and the population that was involved in the TO units; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not all of them. Some were killed. A lot of them were killed [Realtime transcript read in error "skilled"].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. One moment, Mr. Krgovic, because line 9, page 28, the transcript does not reflect the witness's answer, which was "yes." Let's go. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: However, most of these people, people from these units, were in Srebrenica, in the enclave at the time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Just one correction. When I asked you about some people on page 28, line 12, you said that some of them were killed. And you said something else as well. This -- the transcript the wording is "A lot of them were skilled." Is that what you were saying?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Many were killed by shells in attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that in Srebrenica sometime around -- around that time before the arrival of the UN, there was also a military police unit?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that there was one in Srebrenica, but I don't know. In any case, they never entered our villages where we had our TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And did you ever go to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe once a month when I went to see my sister or on some other business. I didn't have time. I had land to farm, and I had my family. So I paid more attention to the land, to sold something, to have something to eat than to go roam around Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that at one point in time, the commander of the military police unit was Mirzet Halilovic? Are you familiar with this name?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then he was replaced, by Atif Krdzic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know this Atif.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, in the column that was formed in Susnjari, were there also people from those units and the villages that I just listed?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, I am going to move to another topic, and I will take you back to your testimony when you spoke about the behaviour of the soldiers who had captured you towards you. Before this Trial Chamber, you have described them being cruel towards the detainees and all the other people from Srebrenica. That people were beaten up, that some people were taken out, the detainees were taken out and killed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be an understatement to say about these people that they are harden criminals?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how I should call these people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can anticipate what your objection is.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think that question, there is no basis for this witness to have any knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I answer this remark?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course. Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have asked the witness about his experience with the people who behaved in that way, people who beat up the detainees and killed them. Would it be a fair statement to say that they were hardened criminals and slaughterers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's obviously you studied criminology, Mr. Krgovic. I would skip that question and move to your next question. I know where you are heading, it doesn't take much to anticipate, but harden criminals -- your next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my line of questioning is based on the introductory speech by the Prosecutor, page 470, lines 12 and 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Your next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, are you aware of the fact that in Srebrenica, during 1992 and 1993, in the police building there was a military prison under the control of the police where Serb detainees, women, children, and men were held, that they were beaten there, some to death. Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is no relevance as far as I can see to that question. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Relevance. It's being suggested that -- you know, if you're bad, the others are bad. But -- anyway, let's -- let's cut this short. Yes, Mr. Krgovic. What -- the other line, approach that you had in mind. In any case, he has told you that he doesn't know about this maltreatment of prisoners, of Serb prisoners by the Muslim -- Bosnian Muslim military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you allow me a couple more questions, everything will become clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... let's see what the other questions are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, are you aware of the fact that units from Jaglici, Susnjari, the ones that you spoke about and that were with you in the column, from Suceska as well, and also from Potocari, in 1993 had participated in the attack on the Serbian villages of Kravica and Jezestica? On that occasion a war crime was committed.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Apart from his being aware or not aware about the fact, do you expect him to say a war crime was committed on that occasion? Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, you've anticipated my objection. It's -- the term war crimes obviously calls for legal conclusion. Among other things, that is not this witness's province, why he was called.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President and Your Honours , and I don't disagree with you, in fact I agree with you but we have testimony where this witness this witness and the previous witness talk about genocide this and genocide that. That's a legal conclusion also. So you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In their mind, maybe, but I can accept it being stated by -- by a witness in his or her ignorance of the correct significance from a legal approach, but from a lawyer asking the witness to confirm that that was a war crime? Come on. Come on. Let's move to the next question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, are you aware of the fact that on that occasion during that attack, those villages were torched and that some people were killed?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that in the Oric case, it was established that the units that I have just mentioned participated in those attacks?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He doesn't know about the attacks, Mr. Krgovic, so how can you -- how can you expect him to confirm what I and the other Judges may have decided in the Oric case about participating units in the attacks? I don't remember myself, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, but he was a member of one of those units which he confirmed previously on one of the cross- examinations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He has -- you have to live with the consequence of the questions that you put, Mr. Krgovic. You asked him whether he belonged to the Jaglici, Susnjari unit. He told you yes. You have asked him whether he knows about the attacks on Kravica and Jezestica, and he's told you no. So there's no point in asking him any further questions about the participation. I mean, the only other possibility is the units having participated in those attacks and he not being present, which would explain his complete ignorance about those attacks. But whether those attacks took place or not is history. Yes. If you can conclude on this chapter now, please do so. Otherwise, we'll have a break and the break needs to be of 30 minutes this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Just one -- actually, as a matter of fact, Your Honours, I can conclude and then I can resume after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you so much. We'll have a 30- minute break starting from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, let's go back to another topic. When you left Susnjari --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter missed the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The interpreter missed part of the question. What we have in the transcript so far, Mr. Krgovic, is "So let's go back to another topic." And if it's another topic, you don't back to it, you go straight to it, but, "When you left Susnjari," and that's where we -- yes. If you could please help us a little bit and tell us exactly what the rest of the question was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, when you left Susnjari, together with the column, you left the protected area of Srebrenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You went to the enemy territory; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You knew that in that territory there were units of the Bosnian Serb army that were ready to resist you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not know that that was the case on route that we took.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But you did know that there were minefields?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We assumed that there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of the fact that free passage may have been asked for from the command of the Bosnian Serbs by your command?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please confirm that all the attacks on the column took place in the enemy territory?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was an abandoned Muslim zone, Muslim villages that had been torched and destroyed between 1992 and 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Under the control of the army of Bosnian Serbs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Where their units were stationed?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the forest that we travelled through, those units were not stationed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But you did expect a possible attack; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And that's why you carried grenades, in order to protect yourself from such an attack, to defend yourself?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's answered that question more than once and gave other explanations, too, in addition to what you've suggested, so next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, let me put you this question: Will you agree with me when I say that in your column, among the people who were there, there were also individuals who had committed crimes against Bosnian Serbs in the territory of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that. I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I suppose any objection you may have had is now superseded. Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And we come to the last team. Who is cross-examining? Mr. Haynes. Mr. Haynes will be cross-examining you now, Mr. Oric, and he represents Mr. Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, I'm really not going to ask you very many questions at all. You've been asked an awful lot of the questions I was going to ask you, and I'm going to do my very best not to repeat any questions that you've been asked before. Okay? If I do so --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: -- forgive me, it's only because I've forgotten that the question's been asked before. Now, firstly, you were born in 1970, a citizen of Yugoslavia. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you remained a citizen of Yugoslavia for 22 years?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: By 1992, you were living in Srebrenica, or the Srebrenica area, together with your wife and daughter; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you also had parents who lived in the area?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They lived with me in the same house.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: In January of 1992, Croatia effectively became an independent country from Yugoslavia, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I suppose so. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Shortly after that date, you chose to go to Croatia and join the MUP in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I went to work in construction, but there was conflict raging which prevented me from doing so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, this work history and time in Croatia has been delved into in detail, and the question that was just asked was asked and answered previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Haynes has obviously forgotten that that question had been asked before. I let him put it again because I think I know what the next question's going to be. Yes, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I wonder if you could explain your motivation for working for what was effectively a military unit for a foreign country.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's put it even clearer. Let's put it even clearer. In early 1992, when Bosnia and Herzegovina had not yet been declared as an independent state, you were, strictly speaking, still a citizen of Yugoslavia, which was at war with Croatia, and it's being put to you to try and explain to us what your motivation was if you were then a citizen Yugoslavia still, that you go to a country that was at war with your country and you join the MUP, which is being suggested to you had military connotations.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I went to work in construction. I was a construction worker. I had worked in construction before with my father. I joined because I didn't think that would be some -- anything dangerous, that we would stay in town, that we would not go anywhere from town. But when I realised what the situation was, I decided to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we skip over a few months now and move to your membership of a military unit in Srebrenica itself? Okay?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: The 28th Division in Srebrenica comprised seven brigades, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many there were. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: 280th to the 286th inclusive. Those were the brigades in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he's already told you he doesn't know. So what I suggest is that if you want to refer to any particular brigade, then you put direct question relating to that brigade and ask him whether he knows whether it was part of the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm not going to dwell on this at all. It's an introductory question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move to the next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You were a commander of a Diversionary Unit. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, a manoeuvre unit. I was the commander of a manoeuvre squad.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And were you the commander of that squad from the moment you arrived in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. From the moment the UNPROFOR arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You were the commander of that squad for two years prior to leaving Srebrenica in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Was that a unit that carried out missions outside the enclave?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was a squad composed of people from Babuljice and Orahovici villages. We just patrolled the lines between the UNPROFOR checkpoints. That was our mission. In the course of a day, we would patrol the lines between these points to prevent incursion of Serb rebels who sometimes entered the town and fired shots. That happened one evening when they entered Srebrenica and created problems. This was our task. Our manoeuvre unit had a task to patrol those lines, and we didn't go anywhere else. Once we inspected a line, we would go back to our homes and work on our land. That was basically our task.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we move to the days prior to the 11th of July, 1995. You gave evidence in chief a few days ago that the town of Srebrenica was shelled constantly for seven days. Is that your account of events?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said approximately. I don't know exactly how many days, but approximately. In any case, this shelling lasted day in, day out.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You've answered my next question. How many shells would you anticipate landed on the town centre of Srebrenica? Hundreds, thousands?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It will be thousands.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Were there many dead and injured civilians during the week prior to the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you that. On the first day of attack, I was in Srebrenica at my sister's, and after that I never returned to Srebrenica, so I really wouldn't know how many people were either injured or killed in Srebrenica. I really wouldn't know how many and how that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you notice when you returned to your sister's much destruction of property as a result of this consistent shelling?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, on day one of the attack, I was at my sister's, and the centre of town was being shelled. The houses and buildings there were being targeted. I did not have much time to observe, because I went back home very quickly after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Moving on, on the 11th of July at Susnjari, and you may have answered this before, you formed into brigades before leaving the area, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an attempt to do that, to form the brigades, but it will failed because nobody knew where people were. In any case, the armed troops that went at the front, they were treated as a brigade to accompany the command. As for the rest, nobody knew where people were, where the brigades were, where the companies were, where their commanders were. Everybody was dispersed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I want to move on now to your being held captive in Bratunac. You said that while you were held captain in Bratunac you were guarded by military policemen.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was captured in Konjevic Polje, and I spent the night in Bratunac. That would be my only correction. And I would say yes to that question. We were guarded by the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you were able to identify them as military policemen in reference to the insignia that they wore?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can you describe that for me?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you want me to describe?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What shape is it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: VP, the military police?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes. What shape is the badge?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was round.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It was round. Colour?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And with an inscription at the bottom, but in any case, there were capital letters, big letters, VP. I can't remember exactly. There were some colours on the badge, but I can't remember what colours were those.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Any other writing that you can remember on the badge?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I couldn't see very well. They were at the front of the bus and I was in the back, but I could spot the big letters, "military police."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we come now to the gymnasium where you were held. Is that a building from which you say you could see out of the windows?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You couldn't see out of the windows?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't see out of the windows. The windows were on the top of the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I want, please, to revisit very briefly your evidence about what you said happened to you at the execution site. You said, I think, that you and those who were with you were shot at about 1.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know when exactly it all started. It may have been around noon or in the afternoon. I wouldn't know the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did you then lie there until you fainted?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was playing dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But you actually passed out at some stage? You lost consciousness?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if I had fallen asleep or lost consciousness. I don't exactly remember what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And when you came round from having lost consciousness, the shooting had finished?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was still going on. They were still bringing in people. I don't know exactly how many, but they were still bringing in people and executing them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I want to be clear that -- what you're saying here. Are you saying that after you passed out and came round again the shooting was still going on?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, just one or two more things. Firstly, in answer to a question from His Honour the Judge a couple of days ago, you said that you neither -- you did not understand written English; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: On the 12th of August of 1995, you made a witness statement together with a Prosecution investigator called Susan Castro. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember. I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What was significant about it was that you drew a number of sketches for her.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I drew a sketch of the school in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And other things. You drew a sketch of an excavating machine and the centre -- and the school at which you were held prisoner at the end.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can I be clear what you're saying about that? Did you actually make the drawings yourself?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I made the drawings myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did you --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did you write upon them any writing that we see in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it was written in Bosnian, then it was my handwriting probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But are you saying that you did not write anything on those drawings that appears in English?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You didn't -- you didn't write any of the English on those drawings?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I wonder, through e-court, whether we could just have a quick look at Prosecution release document number 26. Prosecution release document number 26.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is this the document you wanted to refer the witness to?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because I have a hunch it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But it is because I got the same document on my screen before it was shown by the staff here, and I got the same document as they did. So I think it's a question of reference. Do you have the ERN number? Maybe we can trace it from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It's also 3D7. We can stop at that page just for a moment, and if we can blow it up and look at the bottom it would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That's your signature there at the bottom, "Oric Mevludin," isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And immediately after your signature are your initials OM?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And when you append your initials to anything, that's how you put them down, isn't it, "Oric" first, "Mevludin" second, OM?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You don't put MO, do you? You put OM?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends how I feel. I don't think this is so significant.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, I'd like now to go to page 6998 in that exhibit, please. It's 6981 there, so we need to move on seven pages. No, not that one. That's 6995. One back. Perfect. Can we blow that up for the within, please. Now, this is one of the drawings that you made with Miss or Mrs. Castro. Can we look at the top there, please. Underneath the moon-shaped article there's some writing in your language, isn't there? Somebody will help me as to what it says. Does it say "Suma faust"?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can read it Faust. I read it "forest."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But is that in your writing?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The handwriting -- my handwriting is "Suma," and the lady wrote it in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And what does "Suma" mean? If I can have the interpreter's help and translate Suma.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, "forest."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In other words, they didn't have Goethe and Mephistopheles on their mind, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
